LESSON: DIVERSITY AND INTERPERSONAL SKILLS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People and Relationships
Topic 3.5: Diversity and interpersonal skills

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Diversity and interpersonal skills. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we demonstrate respect and appreciation of social cultural diversity and inclusion?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain ways of building a healthy self- esteem in diverse social cultural society
2. describe the impact of emotions on self and others
3. appreciate social cultural diversities in Kenya

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: DIVERSITY AND INTERPERSONAL SKILLS
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Diversity and interpersonal skills helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: DIVERSITY AND INTERPERSONAL SKILLS
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Explain ways of building a healthy self- esteem in diverse social cultural society

What this means
In this part you learn to explain ways of building a healthy self- esteem in diverse social cultural society. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain ways of building a healthy self- esteem in diverse social cultural society.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Diversity and interpersonal skills” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain ways of building a healthy self- esteem in diverse social cultural society. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe the impact of emotions on self and others

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the impact of emotions on self and others. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the impact of emotions on self and others.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Diversity and interpersonal skills.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the impact of emotions on self and others. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate social cultural diversities in Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate social cultural diversities in Kenya. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate social cultural diversities in Kenya.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate social cultural diversities in Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Diversity and interpersonal skills is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Diversity and interpersonal skills” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: explain ways of building a healthy self- esteem in diverse social cultural society)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Diversity and interpersonal skills. (skill: describe the impact of emotions on self and others)

Example 3: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take. (skill: appreciate social cultural diversities in Kenya)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Diversity and interpersonal skills to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain ways of building a healthy self- esteem in diverse social cultural society.
3. Practise this skill: describe the impact of emotions on self and others.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate social cultural diversities in Kenya.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Diversity and interpersonal skills from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Diversity and interpersonal skills: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Diversity and interpersonal skills?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we demonstrate respect and appreciation of social cultural diversity and inclusion?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Diversity and interpersonal skills means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain ways of building a healthy self- esteem in diverse social cultural society.
5. Be able to: describe the impact of emotions on self and others.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
